items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: Yeah, Buddy Christian. He had plenty women, huh?

ctx.x: Funny fellas, huh? Funny fellas, huh?

Yeah. Says the piano player was funny fellas, huh? Yeah. Yeah. Most of them like Tony Jackson and all of them, you know, like that. And I forget, there was about five or six of them, you know. They said Buddy Christian was one, but they were right enough. They said he wouldn't, you know. He died like one. Yeah, Buddy Christian. He had plenty women, huh? Yeah.
He had plenty women, huh? Yeah.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: Oh, Buddy Christian? Yeah, we used to go around them little girls, and he used to have stock of music, and he'd make them little girls play it.

ctx.x: Let's ask you about Buddy Christian again.

You want to talk about Buddy Christian again? Oh, Buddy Christian? Yeah, we used to go around them little girls, and he used to have stock of music, and he'd make them little girls play it. And after they played, they'd make them play it again. Then he'd sit down and catch in the same key. And he couldn't read the tone, you know. But he'd catch it in the same key, and that made everybody think he could read. But people that know music know that he made the right chords, you know, when he was playing. But that's…
Ask him who his favorite trombone players were in those days, way back.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: Me and him used to do the same thing, because I was a young guy, school guy.

ctx.x: Didn't know his father. Did you know his father?

Did you know his father? Oh, what you mean, chronically? Yeah. Yeah. No, I didn't know Big Eye Louis. I didn't know his daddy. Then I got another Big Eye Louis Robinson piano player. Just told about him, eh? Yeah. Yeah. He was good, but he used to say he played too long like a woman, you know. But when I came up to learn, he wasn't much. He was good in his days. All them fellas were getting, just like if I come out that night, and he's young, she's good. They say I was good in my days, I can't make it these days.…
Ask him where Louis Armstrong got his style.
